text.p: SLM International Inc said Monday its plan of reorganization become effective Monday cancelling the company's common stock.

As a result of the reorganization, confirmed in late January by the Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware, the majority of the company's existing debt has been converted into 100 percent of the equity of the reorganized entity.
All securities of the company, including its common stock, have been canceled and 6.5 million shares of new common stock have been issued, SLM said.
The company said its former common stockholders received warrants to purchase shares of new common stock at a rate of one warrant for every 67 outstanding shares of common stock.

SLM, a manufacturer of hockey products under the CCM and Tacks brand names, also said it entered into a new credit agreement with Chase Manhattan Bank, and one of the company's Canadian subsidiaries entered into a credit agreement with Chase Manhattan Bank of Canada.
The maximum amount of loans and letters of credit that may be outstanding under the credit agreements is $74 million.
The company said it also issued $29.5 million principal amount of 14 percent senior secured notes due April 1, 2004.
